historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr (FY2020-FY2025, 6.4%) shaded to 5.0%: unit growth of ~7-9%/yr on the store base is diluted by new-store productivity and by comps now guided to -1.7% for FY2026 with Q4 at -2% to -4%; the equity CAGR (9.7%) is inflated by retained earnings on a buyback-shrunk share count and the 3-year figures start from the FY2022 post-COVID trough. Shaded from 6.0% in the 2026-09-28 build after the FY2026 net-sales guide fell to +4.3% (52-week) from 4.5-6.5%.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 3yr CAGR (30.5%) is nearly 3x revenue 3yr CAGR (11.2%): FY2022-FY2025 EPS growth came from the EBITDA margin expanding from 7.6% to 9.6% and diluted shares falling from 109.1m to 98.7m, not from top-line growth. Equity 5yr CAGR (9.7%) also exceeds revenue 5yr (6.4%) by more than 30%. Both tailwinds are treated as realised and partly reversing: FY2026 EPS is guided down ~10% (~$4.80 incl. the 53rd week, ~$4.64 without, vs $5.36) and margins are modelled below FY2024, with the share count held flat. FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF (SBC-deducted) series: FY2020 owner FCF $357.7m -> FY2025 $436.6m, FY2022 $230.7m -> FY2025 $436.6m; the owner series grows slightly slower than reported FCF over 5 years (4.1% vs 4.7%) because SBC doubled from $14.3m to $31.1m.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs are unchanged from the 2026-09-28 build (FY0 is still FY2025; the CSV adds Q1-Q3 FY2026 but no new annual row). FY2020 (COVID) is a high starting base for the 5-year figures and FY2022 a low one for the 3-year figures, so neither is a clean trend -- the FY2019-FY2025 six-year revenue CAGR is 7.7%. 39-week FY2026 owner FCF (OCF $555m - capex $284m - SBC $19m = ~$252m) is down ~28% on the same period of FY2025, on higher capex and lower EBIT.

scenario_narratives.base: Sprouts is a unit-growth story whose comp engine has stalled and whose margin is now being spent to restart it: after +7.3% comps in FY2025 the company has printed -1.7%, -1.0% and -0.9%, guides Q4 at -2% to -4% on traffic down 3.3%, and on 2026-10-28 cut FY2026 EPS to ~$4.80 (incl. the 53rd week) while announcing a broader price reset for January 2027 with only an 'above 5%' FY2027 EBIT-margin floor (vs ~6.4% FY2026, 7.8% FY2025). The base case takes management at its word: FY2027 EBIT 5.5% on revenue that is flat-ish after lapping the 53rd week, then a partial recovery -- comps back to +1-1.5%, unit growth ~7% fading, EBIT rebuilding to ~6.1% (the FY2024 level) by FY2030 and no further. Capex stays above D&A for a growing store base, cash taxes normalise to 24%, and the owner-FCF margin matures at ~4.0% (vs ~4.9% in the prior build). The axes that matter are (1) whether the price reset restores traffic or only resets margin, (2) whether the new CEO keeps opening 35-40 stores a year or slows to protect cash, and (3) how much of the FY2024-25 margin was the +7-11% comp cycle rather than the format.
scenario_narratives.bull: The January 2027 affordability reset works the way key-value-item investment has for other grocers: transactions turn positive within two to three quarters, comps run +3% in FY2028-29 on a smaller-store format whose unit economics are intact (ROIC 16% even in a down year), openings hold at ~40/yr with the Northeast proving out, and revenue compounds at 7-8% mid-decade. The margin dips in FY2027 and then rebuilds to a 9.6% pre-SBC EBITDA margin (EBIT ~7.2%) on fixed-cost leverage, private label past 30% of sales and the completed self-distribution network -- below the FY2025 peak. With the stock at ~10x the reset EPS, net cash and $537m of buyback authorization, both earnings and the multiple recover.
scenario_narratives.bear: The affordability gap to Walmart, Costco and Aldi is structural for a secondary-destination grocer, and management has admitted its pricing strategy 'has not delivered'; the reset buys margin away without buying traffic back. Comps stay negative through FY2028, the new CEO (January 2027, with the CTO seat vacant) slows openings to ~25/yr, the FY2027 'above 5%' EBIT floor becomes the permanent level (~4.8-5.0%), revenue growth is 2-3%, the owner-FCF margin settles near 3.4%, and the business is a slow-growth grocer capped at 14x owner FCF. The securities class action (amended complaint due 2026-11-10) is a tail risk on top of this path, not inside it; Harvest Sherwood is settled and no longer a risk.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Sprouts as a self-funded store-growth compounder whose comps have gone negative and whose margin is being reinvested in price, not as the +7% comp business of FY2025 and not as a broken retailer. The owner-FCF build charges SBC (~$25m, 0.3% of sales) in the flows and holds the share count flat; buybacks ($472m in FY2025, ~$330m in FY2026 to date) are how the count stays flat, not a source of value. FY2026 is the guided year (53 weeks, comps -1.7%, EBIT ~$605m, EPS ~$4.80, capex up on a completed distribution centre); FY2027 is management's 'above 5%' EBIT-margin year with the 53rd week lapped; after that growth is new-store arithmetic on a 500-store base fading from ~5.5% to 3%, margins rebuild only to the FY2024 level, and a 10-year horizon lets the owner-FCF margin mature (~4.0%) before a Gordon terminal at 2.5% on a 9% USD WACC. Leases are in the flows under ASC 842; only finance obligations are debt.
key_risks_to_valuation: Comps and traffic: every 1pp of sustained comp is roughly 1pp of revenue growth AND ~30-40bp of EBITDA margin through fixed-cost leverage; the bear path (comps -2%/-1% through FY2028, floor-level margin) is what takes the value to the high $40s -- roughly today's price.

The price reset is a one-way bet on margin: ~90bp of Q4 gross-margin deleverage is committed before any traffic response is visible; if traffic does not respond the base case's recovery from 7.9% to 8.5% pre-SBC EBITDA does not happen (each 50bp of mature margin is ~$5/share).
Unit growth: no FY2027 opening target; the base assumes ~32-35 stores/yr (~7% unit growth) fading, the bull ~40, the bear ~25. The ~10% aspiration is not in any scenario.
New-store productivity and cannibalisation as openings move into the Northeast; the base assumes new stores keep earning near-chain-average returns (ROIC incl. leases 16.1%, down from 18.3%).

Capex: FY2026 gross capex ~$340m is 3.6% of sales vs 2.8% in FY2025; the base assumes it eases to 2.8% -- if openings and the tech/supply-chain programme keep capex at 3.5% the owner-FCF margin matures ~0.7pp lower (~$9/share).
Cash tax: the model ramps to 24%; the 10-Q already notes shrinking stock-comp and transferable-credit benefits, so a return of those benefits is upside, not risk.

Leadership: CEO handover (Nick Konat, 2027-01-04) coincides with the price reset, the CTO left 2026-10-12 with no successor, and the executive chairman has a 10b5-1 selling plan; the securities class action (amended complaint due 2026-11-10) is an unmodelled tail.

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K consolidated cash flow statement, equity-based compensation add-back $31,103k (SFM_Annual_FY2025.txt cash flow statement). The 10-K discloses no separate line for taxes paid on net-share settlement, so the add-back is the whole charge; no combined adjusted-EBITDA figure is published. FY0 (FY2025) anchors are unchanged from the 2026-09-28 build; the Q3-2026 10-Q (SFM_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt:946) shows 39-week SBC of $19,465k vs $22,045k, with Q3 alone $3,798k (a performance-award true-down after the guidance cut), so FY2026 SBC runs ~0.27% of sales and the forward path is set at 0.30%.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchase of common stock $471.9m (10-K financing activities); 39 weeks of FY2026 $299.2m (3.9m shares at ~$77.65 average) plus ~$30m through 2026-10-26, $537m authorization remaining, FY2026 guide 'more than $300m'. The flat share count is being funded in cash (repurchaser), well in excess of SBC; at $49.7 the same dollars retire ~50% more shares than they did in H1, which is an upside to the flat-count convention, not a modelled source of value.
inputs.share_count_basis: Q3-2026 10-Q diluted weighted-average shares 93.666m (13 weeks ended 2026-09-27; basic 93.128m, equivalents 0.54m). Cover page shows 92.23m basic shares at 2026-10-26 after October repurchases (~92.8m diluted) -- that count is paired with cash the model does not have, so the September figure is used with the September balance sheet. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count).
inputs.fiscal_year_end: Sunday nearest 31 December (52/53-week year; FY2025 ended 2025-12-28; FY2026 is a 53-week year ending 2027-01-03)
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-30T20:00:01Z regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API); Friday close, two days after the Q3 release and guidance cut, not an after-hours print
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Risk-free ~4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.0 (grocery staples with specialty-retail sensitivity) gives a cost of equity ~9.2%; no funded debt (revolver undrawn, only $133m of finance-lease and build-to-suit finance obligations) so WACC ~9.0%. Applied uniformly to all three scenarios: risk is charged once, through the probability weights, not through per-scenario discount rates. Unchanged from 2026-09-28; the guidance cut is an earnings-path event, not a capital-structure or currency event.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842: operating-lease rent (~$2.10bn of operating lease liabilities at Q3-2026) is a straight-line SG&A charge, so reported EBITDA and OCF are already post-rent -- leases are in the flows. Only finance-lease liabilities ($11.0m) and the build-to-suit finance obligations ($118.6m; the Northern California DC completed Q3-2026, whose payments are split into interest expense and financing principal) are treated as debt: $133.1m total at 2026-09-27 (SFM_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt:846,849,1081-1083). Not both.
inputs.tax_note: GAAP effective rate 24.0% FY2025; 39-week FY2026 cash taxes paid $97.5m on $542m of EBIT = 18%, still flattered by stock-comp deductions and transferable tax credits, though the 10-Q notes both benefits shrinking. Cash rate ramps 21% -> 24% (21% federal + state) by year 4, unchanged from the prior build.
inputs.notes: UPDATE of the 2026-09-28 Drivers build after the Q3-2026 10-Q and the 2026-10-28 guidance cut. Model unchanged: owner-FCF component DCF (routing table row: operating company, consumer). SFM is a US specialty grocer with 504 company-operated stores, no franchising, no NCI, net cash; the standard operating-company route applies. Interest income not stripped: net interest is now a small expense (DC finance obligation) and net cash ($96m) is ~0.2x the owner-FCF base. FY0 stays FY2025 (52 weeks ended 2025-12-28); year 1 is FY2026 (53 weeks), rebuilt to the 2026-10-28 guide: EPS ~$4.80, comps ~-1.7%, EBIT ~$605m, net sales +4.3% on 52 weeks plus a 53rd week of ~$190m sales/~$20m EBIT, net capex ~$310m, 42 net new stores, buybacks $300m+. The 53rd-week basis of the EPS guide was checked arithmetically rather than against the 8-K (not in Extracted): YTD diluted EPS $4.30 + Q4 guide $0.47-0.51 = $4.77-4.81, so $4.80 INCLUDES the 53rd week (~$0.16), and YTD EBIT $542.3m + Q4 ~$63m incl ~$20m from the extra week = $605m -- i.e. the 13-week Q4 EBIT is ~$43m vs $123m a year ago, which is the price investment and 90bp of gross-margin deleverage landing. Year 1 is therefore built at a pre-SBC EBITDA margin of 8.7% (EBIT 6.4% = ~$600m on ~$9.37bn) and +6.4% revenue growth (4.3% + 2.1% from the 53rd week). DRIVER YEARS RE-JUDGED: FY2026 (guidance), FY2027 (management's new >5% EBIT-margin floor replaces the 'flat comps, margin rebuilds' path, and the 53rd-week lap), and the FY2028-30 recovery slope, because the prior paths assumed margins rebuilding to 9.8% from a 9.45% trough and that trough is now 8.7% with a 7.9% FY2027 below it; the matured base margin is cut to 8.5% (EBIT ~6.1%, the FY2024 level, between FY2023's 7.4% and FY2025's 9.9%). Unit growth is treated at ~7%/yr fading, not the ~10% aspiration: no FY2027 unit guide and the CFO said the pace must be balanced against other needs. DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: WACC 9.0%, cash-tax ramp 21->24%, D&A path, working-capital capture 2%, terminal growth 2.5/3.0/2.0 and caps 16/16/14, years 7-10 growth fade (3.0-3.5%) -- the evidence that would move them is a change in funded debt or rates (WACC), a tax-credit or NOL disclosure (tax), a change in the long-run opening cadence or a format change (capex/D&A/fade). SBC % moved 0.35 -> 0.30 on the 39-week actual. Harvest Sherwood was settled for an immaterial amount (July 2026), so the prior key_risk is removed rather than modelled.

bear.rationale: The traffic loss is structural (transactions -3.3% in Q3 against easier compares, share going to Walmart, Costco and Aldi) and the price reset buys little of it back: Q4-2026 comps at the bottom of the guide (-4%, FY2026 +6.2%), FY2027 comps -2% and FY2028 -1% before flattening, while the new CEO slows openings to ~25/yr (unit growth ~5% -> 3%) to protect cash, so FY2027 revenue is +0.5% after the 53rd-week lap and 2-3% thereafter. The FY2027 'above 5%' EBIT floor becomes the level: pre-SBC EBITDA 7.4% in FY2027 (EBIT 5.0%) and 7.3% thereafter (EBIT ~4.8% as D&A rises to 2.2% on the built base), i.e. the FY2023 margin on a bigger store base. Capex falls with the opening cadence to 2.5%. Terminal 2.0%, cap 14x for a no-growth grocer (Gordon at 9%/2% = 14.6x, so the cap binds). Prior bear: 6.0/1.5/2.5/3.0... growth, margin 9.2% -> 8.3% -- roughly what management now guides as the base path.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +6.4% = the guided ~4.3% on 52 weeks (42 net new stores contributing ~6%, comps ~-1.7% with Q4 at -2% to -4%) plus ~2.1% from the 53rd week (~$190m): revenue ~$9.37bn. FY2027 +3.0%: laps the 53rd week (-2.0pp); new stores (FY2026 openings annualising plus ~32-35 openings in FY2027, ~7% unit growth on 504) contribute ~5.5% and comps run ~-0.5% as the January 2027 price reset is deflationary before it rebuilds traffic. FY2028-30 5.5/5.0/4.5% as comps recover to +1-1.5% and unit growth of ~30-35 stores/yr shrinks as a share of a 540-610 store base; fades to 3% by year 8 (unit growth ~3-4%, comps ~inflation). Prior build: 6.7/4.5/6.0/5.5/5.0/4.5/4.0/3.5/3.0/3.0.
base.margin_rationale: EBITDA margin here is pre-SBC. FY2026 8.7% = guided EBIT ~$605m (incl. ~$20m from the 53rd week) + D&A ~$187m (39 weeks $137.7m, Q3 $44.9m) + SBC ~$25m on ~$9.37bn; the implied 13-week Q4 EBIT is ~$43m vs $123m a year ago. FY2027 7.9% = EBIT 5.5% (management's floor is 'above 5%' while funding price, technology, labour and supply-chain spend) + D&A 2.05% + SBC 0.3%. Recovers 20bp/yr to 8.5% by FY2030 (EBIT ~6.1%, the FY2024 level) as the price reset restores some traffic leverage and private label (26%), self-distribution and retail media offset part of the gross-margin give-back; it does NOT return to FY2025's 9.9% -- the FY2024-25 margin was earned on +7-11% comps that have gone. D&A 2.0% -> 2.1% (FY2025 1.8%, Q3-2026 1.95%, rising with the new-store base and the DC that started depreciating in Q3). Capex gross of landlord reimbursements: FY2026 3.6% (~$340m gross vs ~$310m net guide; 39 weeks $284m gross) easing to 2.8% as openings slow relative to the base; stays above D&A because the store base is still growing. Working capital: grocers run negative working capital, so growth releases a little cash -- 2% of the revenue increase. Prior build: 9.45% trough rebuilding to 9.8%.
base.terminal_rationale: 2.5% terminal growth (mature staples retailer, ~inflation); cap 16x owner FCF. At 9%/2.5% Gordon is 15.8x so Gordon binds. Unchanged.

bull.rationale: Q4-2026 lands at the better end of the guide (comps -2%, FY2026 +6.6%) and the January 2027 price reset does what Kroger/Walmart-style key-value-item investment usually does for a grocer: traffic turns within two to three quarters, FY2027 comps +1% (H1 negative, H2 +2-3%), FY2028-29 comps +3% with openings sustained at ~40/yr and the Northeast format proving out, so revenue compounds at 7-8% mid-decade. The FY2027 EBIT margin still dips (8.3% pre-SBC EBITDA = EBIT ~5.9%) because the price investment is front-loaded, then rebuilds to 9.6% (EBIT ~7.2%) on fixed-cost leverage, private-label mix past 30% and full self-distribution -- below the FY2025 peak of 9.9%, which was earned on +7% comps. Capex stays ~3-3.5% for the faster opening cadence. Cap 16x binds (Gordon at 9%/3% = 17.2x). Prior bull: 7.0/6.0/8.0/7.5/7.0... growth, margin to 10.8%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 16x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 30% (from 25%): management has now delivered roughly what the prior bear described (negative comps through FY2027, margin given back to ~8.3%), so the new bear is a further leg -- the floor becomes the level and openings slow -- and with traffic still falling against easier compares, the price reset unproven, a CEO handover in January and the CTO seat vacant, that is a live three-in-ten outcome even though the net-cash balance sheet rules out distress. Bull cut to 20% (from 25%): it needs the price reset to restore traffic AND the margin to rebuild past FY2024, two independent things, with the first having no evidence yet. Base 50%: the unit pipeline (105 executed leases, 160+ approved sites) is funded and the FY2027 margin floor is a stated commitment. Prior split 25/50/25.
probability_weighted.note: Street-basis values are a memo only: SBC is 0.3% of sales, so the house/street band is ~$3/share wide and the regime question is immaterial for SFM.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
